STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Square plates are typically 20-30 cm. This one looks medium-sized, around 24 cm side.
b) Reference: the plate spans roughly the width of the metal frame's inner channel. The bacon strips are about 15-18 cm long each in the photo, so the plate is roughly 1.4-1.5 bacon lengths across, which gives about 22-25 cm.
Reconciled width: 24 cm (area about 576 cm²).

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Bacon, two cooked strips (one longer, about 17 cm; one shorter, about 11 cm, partly broken). Total length about 28 cm of strip, width about 1.2 cm, cooked thickness about 0.2-0.3 cm.

- Thickness: one strip layer, about 0.3 cm (crisp, flat-ish).
- Volume: 40 x 0.3 = 12 ml. Cooked bacon is dense-ish and fatty, so use density 1.0 g/ml, but cooked bacon with rendered fat lost is lighter; take about 0.8 g/ml. Grams: 12 x 0.8 ≈ 10 g.
- Check against typical: two cooked bacon strips usually weigh about 12-16 g. Adopting 14 g to reconcile with the count.

Hidden food: none; plate is otherwise clear (a tiny crumb only).

STEP 4 - No base layer or hidden food. Total about 14 g.

STEP 5 - Cooked bacon, pan-fried: about 540 kcal per 100 g (fat-rich, after rendering). Energy: 14 g x 5.4 ≈ 76 kcal.
